source.title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
source.authors: Kuan Zhang; Yu-Kun Chen; Zhi-Hao Yang; Yue Su; Xiang-Nan Wu; Zi-Rong Chen; Run Luo; Jin-Kun Hou; Tao Tan; Yinhe Zheng; Yi-Ming Li

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether scaling-law behavior extends to multimodal embodied continued pre-training. The study reports strong fitted laws for some held-out losses but finds that OOD loss rises with additional training rather than following a data-scaling law.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation-loss scaling fits and their hold-out predictions, which bear on the claim. Downstream gameplay benchmark scores are not rows here: they do not directly measure the claim versions about loss scaling. Cited language-model scaling results are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study fits a Chinchilla-derived power law (Eq. 3, with an added mixture-share term and floor) to held-out action-token loss of 0.8B–27B multimodal Qwen3.5 models. These models are continued-pretrained on gameplay across a 4×6×5 grid. It also reports hold-out predictions and fitting-ridge analyses. This is a new setting (embodied CPT) bearing on V5, and its fitting analysis bears on V7. It is T3 rather than T5: it does not argue that a version is wrong in its original setting.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that an empirical three-factor law (Chinchilla plus a mixture share and finite floor) fits Minecraft and in-corpus validation losses well and extrapolates about one doubling in size or data. OOD loss does not follow a data-scaling law: it rises after an early gain. Individual exponents are poorly determined (ridges, wide intervals), and strong in-domain fits do not guarantee distant-world play.
record.recipe_differences: This is embodied multimodal continued pre-training, with visual observations and structured action-token targets, rather than text-only language-model pretraining. The authors fit a three-factor empirical law with a mixture-share term and finite floor; they do not estimate compute-optimal parameter/token allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on validation domain and training mixture. The fitted law includes the mixture share; OOD loss behaves oppositely to the in-corpus losses. The authors use a Huber loss on log residuals and report that β and the offset lie on broad fitting ridges for validation losses. Fits and predictions are based on a single training seed.
record.problems: The 120-condition grid uses one training seed, so reported bootstrap uncertainty does not measure seed-to-seed variance. There are only four model sizes, and hold-out predictions span at most one doubling; the results do not establish extrapolation by orders of magnitude. The paper itself reports wide intervals or fitting ridges for some exponents.
record.rows_left_out: No additional loss-scaling results left out. Downstream benchmark scores and comparisons with other models were omitted because they do not directly measure the claim versions recorded here.

untested.parts: Not text pretraining loss. The loss is on gameplay action tokens during continued pre-training of multimodal backbones.
Hold-out predictions span only about one doubling of size or data, not orders of magnitude.
No compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is estimated.
No depth/width or shape comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Image/video generative models, repeated-data pretraining and general fine-tuning/transfer are not tested. Only one setting (embodied gameplay CPT) is tested, with a single seed.
Benchmark scores versus scale are reported qualitatively, but no predictive fit of downstream performance from scale or loss is made.
No comparison with published LM exponents or compute-optimal splits. No parameter-counting variants are tested.

missing.what: Profile ridge: β can be fixed anywhere in 0.15–0.50 (Minecraft) or 0.03–0.30 (in-corpus) with R² within 0.001, while E moves by 0.11–0.14. The α interval is 0.02–0.30. The asymptote is not identifiable.
missing.locator: Appendix C.6, Table 14 and 'Uncertainty of the fits'

missing.what: Restricted baselines: Chinchilla with D=T gives R² 0.925 and with D=rT gives 0.959 on Minecraft S1–S3. On in-corpus loss, D=T gives 0.991 and D=(1−r)T gives 0.955. Forcing η=−β lowers R² to 0.825.
The training-loss law extrapolates with RMSE 0.009 and biased residuals (+0.0078 for 27B, −0.0081 for 1,600 h), attributed to the WSD decay endpoint. This shows schedule dependence.
Backward data hold-out (100–1,600 h → 50 h): RMSE 0.0025/0.0022, R² 0.916/0.967. Held-out mixture S4 on Minecraft loss: RMSE 0.0057.
Training-loss fit L = ES + A/N^α + B/T^β: R² 0.980, α 0.39, β 0.07.
Raw curve directions: 19/20 Minecraft curves fall (the exception is S5); the 4 S1 in-corpus curves rise.
missing.locator: Appendix C.6, 'Which losses admit a scaling law'

missing.what: Benchmark behaviour with scale: GameWorld degrades with more data at 27B, and MCU/ViZDoom gains diminish beyond 9B. This is qualitative evidence on downstream predictability.

record.verdict_notes: The study cites the original sources and adapts the Chinchilla fitting procedure, but it is not an original source. All results come from a single training seed. Bootstrap intervals reflect which conditions enter the fit, not seed variance. The V2 link was rejected because hold-outs span one doubling. Downstream benchmark comparisons with frontier models were correctly excluded from the rows.

versions.untested_parts: The models are embodied multimodal agents trained on visual observations and action tokens, not a study of held-out text-pretraining loss in language models.
The study predicts held-out checkpoints across one doubling of model size or data budget, not runs orders of magnitude larger.
The study does not identify loss-minimizing parameter and token allocations at fixed compute or fit their growth with compute.
It varies backbone size, but does not compare depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Tests embodied gameplay continued pre-training and action-token validation loss; does not test image/video generative models, repeated-data pretraining, fine-tuning, or transfer generally.
The paper reports gameplay benchmark scores but does not test whether downstream performance is predictable from scale or pretraining loss.
Does not compare the original language-model studies’ exponents or compute-optimal allocations; its fit-sensitivity evidence concerns this study’s embodied CPT loss fits.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Minecraft and in-corpus held-out loss (worlds in the training corpus), 0.8B–27B, 50–1,600 h
source_check.reason: R1–R2 and R5–R8 confirm strong fits and modest-range predictions for the extended power-law form. The reason's claim of no systematic bias is too strong: Table 14 gives positive 27B mean-residual intervals excluding zero, although their magnitudes are small.

relationships.condition: Validation worlds absent from the training data (OOD set; also Minecraft loss under S5 and in-corpus loss under S1)
relationships.reason: OOD loss rises over training in all 20 curves and the fitted β≈0 (R3, R4). The text also reports flat S5 Minecraft curves and rising S1 in-corpus curves, which require a mixture-share term and floor beyond plain Chinchilla. This is limits_scope rather than challenges because it is distribution-shifted evaluation.
relationships.display_finding: All 20 out-of-distribution loss curves rose during training with β≈0, while flat S5 Minecraft loss and rising S1 in-corpus loss required a mixture-share term and loss floor.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Validation worlds absent from the training data (OOD set; also Minecraft loss under S5 and in-corpus loss under S1)
source_check.reason: R3–R4 establish rising OOD loss and no decreasing data term. Appendix C.6 also identifies nearly flat Minecraft loss without Minecraft training and rising in-corpus loss without pool-game training. These measured conditions qualify the extension to gameplay CPT.

relationships.condition: Fitting of Eq. 3 and its alternatives on this grid
relationships.reason: Fit quality changes with functional form (R9, R10; Table 11, R² 0.925–0.989). From the text: β trades off against E along a ridge (0.15–0.5), α's interval spans 0.02–0.30, and the WSD decay makes the training-law extrapolation biased.
relationships.display_finding: Fit R² ranged from 0.925 to 0.989 across functional forms, β traded off against E over 0.15–0.5, α's interval spanned 0.02–0.30, and WSD decay biased training-law extrapolation.

source_check.label: supports

relation.reason: The study fits and compares scaling laws, tests held-out predictions, and measures conditions where decreasing loss with additional data fails.

tranche.reason: The study directly tests scaling laws in a new setting: multimodal embodied-agent continued pretraining on gameplay, with in-corpus fits and measured transfer boundaries.

source_check.notes: Bootstrap intervals measure sensitivity to sampled conditions on a single-seed grid, not training-seed variability. Size extrapolation is 9B → 27B (3×), and data extrapolation is 800 → 1,600 h (2×); neither tests orders-of-magnitude extrapolation.

statements.correction: In-corpus loss decreases with hours under diverse mixtures S2–S5; all four S1 in-corpus curves rise. All 20 OOD curves finish higher at 1,600 h than at 50 h.
statements.problem: The gameplay summary omits the mixture condition: in-corpus loss rises under Minecraft-only S1 training.
